title: Battery black-mass recycling recovery rates
bottleneck: Recycling spent batteries into battery-grade nickel, cobalt, and lithium remains inefficient: pyrometallurgy loses lithium to slag, hydrometallurgy is chemical- and water-intensive, and direct recycling that preserves cathode crystal structure works only on pristine, single-chemistry feedstocks. Mixed, degraded real-world packs defeat the cleanest processes, and economics still favor mining when metal prices dip.
why_it_blocks: Without high-recovery recycling, the battery transition locks in ever-growing mining demand and its environmental toll. A circular supply chain is also the main hedge against the cobalt, nickel, and lithium price spikes that threaten EV affordability.
current_state: Hydrometallurgical plants are scaling in China, Europe, and North America with recovery rates above 90 percent for nickel and cobalt, though lithium recovery lags. Direct recycling remains pre-commercial, and collection logistics for end-of-life packs are still patchy.
